evidence: Tac. Dial. 34.2–3: hujus omnibus dictiōnibus interesse
M-O s.v. attend, take (a class, course): lēctiōnibus interesse
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to be present at, take part in, attend”. For taking part, see be involved.

evidence: Ov. Tr. 4.10.11: Lūcifer ambōrum nātālibus adfuit īdem
M-O s.v. attend, go to (a university, school)
terms.comment: Classically to visit a place or a person often (Lewis & Short: “to visit or resort to frequently, to frequent”); see go to school.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.200 (Lewis & Short): maximā … frequentiā cīvium
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “a numerous attendance … (class.; a favorite expression of Cicero)”.
Latin attendō is to pay attention (see pay attention!), never to be present at something.

phrases.latin: hunc sectārī, hunc prōsequī, hujus omnibus dictiōnibus interesse … adsuēscēbat
phrases.english: He would get used to following him about, escorting him, being present at all his speeches.

phrases.latin: Lūcifer ambōrum nātālibus adfuit īdem: ūna celebrāta est per duo lība diēs
phrases.english: The same morning star was there at both our births: one day was kept with two birthday cakes.
Will you be at the dinner tomorrow?
